keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height of 120 m is measured as the distance to the closest point of the Earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall man-made obstacle (over 105 m), the party responsible for the obstacle can request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or could transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy on impact) — this also applies to toys. Under 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to collect personal data, unless it counts as a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.
In Iceland the minimum age is 16 — exceptions apply to a C0-class drone in subcategory A1, a privately built drone under 250 g, or flights supervised by a certified remote pilot.

During volcanic eruptions, Almannavarnir/Samgöngustofa may impose temporary restrictions on drone flights — restrictions can extend up to 1,500 ft, and entire areas (e.g. the Reykjanes Peninsula during the July 2025 eruption) can be closed completely while activity lasts. Always check current volcanic activity before flying.

From 17 May 2026, Náttúruverndarstofnun (not the aviation authorities) issues permits only for commercial drone flights in 27 protected areas. The restrictions come in three tiers: 15 areas all year round (incl. Gullfoss, Geysir, Goðafoss, Skógafoss, Dyrhólaey, Látrabjarg and the Mývatn and Laxá conservation area), 11 areas from 1 May to 15 September (incl. Snæfellsjökull National Park, Dimmuborgir, Hornstrandir and Dynjandi) and Friðlandið að Fjallabaki from 15 June to 15 September. Permits for research, monitoring, filming, commercial photography and events requiring a permit are still granted. Þingvellir and Vatnajökull National Park are not on this list and have their own rules.

Flying closer than 150 m to sensitive structures is prohibited: power plants, substations, Alþingi, the President's residence, ministries, embassies, police stations, prisons and hospitals, unless permitted by the owners or those in control of them.

In the open category you must keep the drone within your own unaided line of sight (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, with clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a special exemption, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

Flying without permission from the airport operator is prohibited at airports, within airport areas and within the restricted zones around scheduled-service airports — the restricted zones are the areas shown on the map in the app (in many places about 5 km). Within a restricted zone, however, you may fly without special permission if you fly below the height of the highest obstacles within 50 metres of the drone's flight path. Permission: ISAVIA for Keflavík Airport, Innanlandsflugvellir ehf. for other scheduled-service airports.
Difficult wind conditions: in Iceland the wind often exceeds drone safety limits
importantNotes: Active volcanic eruption areas may have temporary flight bans — check before every flight

From 17 May 2026, Náttúruverndarstofnun grants permits only for commercial drone flights in 27 protected areas — some all year round, others only during the summer months. Check the list for each area on nattura.is.
Icelandic weather is volatile — the wind often exceeds drone limits
Bird nesting season (May–August): additional restrictions in many areas
Iceland is in the EEA but not the EU — EASA rules apply through the EEA Agreement
